saints.name: St. Romuald
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A nobleman of Ravenna who became a hermit and founded the Camaldolese, wedding the monastic and eremitic life…
biography: Born about 951 at Ravenna into the ducal house of the Onesti, Romuald was about twenty when he saw his father Sergius kill a kinsman in a duel over property. In penance he fled to the Benedictine abbey of San Apollinare in Classe, and after three years, finding its observance too mild, placed himself under a hermit named Marinus near Venice.

About 978 he persuaded Peter Orseolo, the doge of Venice, to resign his office in repentance, and followed him to the abbey of Cuxa in the Pyrenees, living as a hermit nearby. Back in Italy he spent some four decades wandering the peninsula, reforming monasteries and planting or renewing colonies of hermits, Val di Castro, Fonte Avellana, and Sitria among them.

About 1012, in the Casentino hills above Arezzo, a nobleman named Maldolus gave him the estate where he built Camaldoli, the field of Maldolus, whence the name, joining a hermitage of solitary cells to a monastery of the common life. From this wedding of the two ways grew the Camaldolese Benedictines. Romuald died at Val di Castro on 19 June 1027.
